NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN, that the next GUNER&L QUARTER SESSIONS of the Peace for the COUNTY OF CHESTER will be holden at the Castle of Chester, in and for the said County, on MONDAY, the sth day of January next, at Half-past Eleven o'clock in the Forenoon, when the Grand Jury will be empannelled. The hearing of all appeals arising within the Hundreds of Broxton, Eddisbury, Nantwich, and Wirral, forming the, Chester District, and the trials of all. prisoners committed from such Hundreds, will take place at such Sessions. The Grand and Petty Jury or the Chester District must be in attendance at the Castle of Chester. at the opening of the Court on MONDAY, the 51h day of January next, at Half-past Eleven o'clock in the Eoreno.m.. WHEREAS at the General Quarter Sessions of the Peace, holden at Nether K7l sford. in and for the County of Chester, on Monday, the 13th day of October, 1893, a Provisional Order was made in the words following, that is to say— At the General Quarter Sessions of the Peace of our Lady the Queen holden at Nether Knutsford, in and for the Countyof Chester, on Monday, the 13th day of October, 1890. WHEREAS a propo.al In writing, dated the 13th Septem- ber, 1890, hath been alt hefore this Court under the hands of the lionours.ble, Cecil Thomas Parker, Benjamin Chaffers Roberts, Esquire, John Thompson, Esquire, James Sweten- ham, Esquire. and The devoiamd Edward Augustus Pitcairn Campbell, five of Her IVisjes,y's Justices of the Peace for the County of Chester, to vary the existing boundaries o' the Highway District of the Western Division of the Hundred of Broxton by including within etch District and adding thereto the Township of Huntington, in the said County ef Chester. NOW IT IS ORDERED by this Court, upon consideration of such proposal, that the said Township of HuntingtoN shall, from and after the 25th day of Match. 1891, be added to and form part of the said Highway District of the Western Division of the Hundred of 13roxton, in the said County, for all the purposes ot the Highway Acts. AND IT IS FURTHER ORDERED that the said Township of Huntington shall be entitled to elect one Waywarden to form part of the Highway Board for the said Highway District. AND IT IS ALSO FURTHER ORDERED that the said Township ef Hunting- ton so included in such Highway District as aforesaid, shall not be liable to contribute to any Debts or Loans contracted by the said Highway Board for such Highway District prior to the said 25th day of March, 1891. AND THIS COURT doth hereby appoint the General Quarter Sessions of the Peaco to be held at CHESTER CASTLE, in and for the said County of Chester, on MONDAY, the 6th day of January, 1891, for the purpose of taking into consideration the Confirmation of the Pro- visional Order hereby made. NOTICE IS HEREBY ALSO GI -YEN, that the Confirma- tion of the said Provisional Order by a Final Order will be taken into consideration by the Justices at the Court of General Quarter Sessions to be held at CHESTER CASTLE aforesaid, On MONDAY, the sth day of January next. THE COURT will be Adjourned to the Court House, Nether Knutsford, on WEDNDSDAY, the 7th day of January next, at Eleven o'clock in the Forenoon. The hearing of all appeals arising within the Hundreds of Bucklow,Maccieslield, and Northwich, forming the Knutsford District, and the trials of all prisoners committed from the last mentioned Hundreds will takeplace at such Adjourned Sessions. The Grand Jury for the Knutsford District must be in attendance at the Court House, Knutsford. at the opening of the Court on WEDNESDAY, the 7th day of January next, at Eleven o'clock in the Forenoon. REGINALD POTTS. Clerk of the Peace for the County of Chester. ' Chester, 16th December, 1890.

LIBELLING JUSTICES. 112 the Queen's Bench, on Monday, Mr. Justice Stephen Sentenced Richard Masters and Frederick Masters, prin- ters and publishers of the "Kent Messenger" and "Maidstone Telegraph," to a fine of £l5O each for pub- lishing a libel on certain Dartford justices. TERRIBLE ACCIDENT IN BOMBAY. , THIRTY PERSONS KILLED. ' Ramnav, WEDNESDAY.—A large four-storey house in the native quarter of the city suddenly collapsed early this morning, burying over 100 men, women, :and children who were asleep at the time. Upwards -of 30 persons were killed, and many dreadfully niured. RAILWAY ACCIDENT AT BOLTON. On Wednesday morning a collision occurred between a goods train and a passenger train at Bullfield siding in Bolton, by which the main line to the north was blocked for two hours, the traffic being much delayed. Both the passengers and goods train were much damaged, and the passenger guard had a narrow escape, he jumping from the train a few moments before the collision occurred. • • A BOLTON CLERGYMAN AND HIS TENANT. On Tuesday night, the Mayor of Bolton, the Vicar, Mr. John Fielding, J. P., and two other gentlemen were ap- pointed by public meeting a committee to investigate a tharge of cruelty preferred against the Rev. T. T. Berger, vicar of St. James, for turning out a family of cottage tenants when the husband was dying of consumption. Mr. Berger asserts that the family forced his action by their own misconduct. THE SERPENT INQUIRY. The court of inquiry into the loss of' the Serpent was -opened on Tuesday, on board H.M.S.Black Prince. The survivors were present, but the Deputy Judge-Advocate of the Fleet announced that there was no charge against them. Communications from Lieutenant-Commander Galloway were read giving the survivors' description of the wreck. It denied the suggestions of panic, and de- clared that the crew died manfully, wishing each other good-bye. The Court on Wednesday found that the ship was seaworthy and properly equipped, and attributed her loss to an error of judgment on the part of those respon- sible for her navigation. SEQUEL TO AN ELOPEMENT. TRIAL FOR MURDER. At Stafford Assizes, on Tuesday, John Wise, aged thirty-four, steel-fitter, was charged with murdering Mary Davis, at Sedgley. His wife eloped with Mrs. Davis's son and he vainly followed to Liverpool with a loaded revolver. He then asked Mrs. Davis for informa- tion, saying," I would treat them like that," presented a revolver, which went off, and shot her. The jury con- victed Wise of manslaughter, but strongly recommended him to mercy. Justice Mathew sentenced him to six days' imprisonment, and Wise was at once released. THE MARK'S LIBEL CASE. On Wednesday SirC. Russell continued his reply for the prosecutor in the libel prosecution of Mr. G. Butterfield, at the Old Bailey. He denied the imputations of frauds against Mr. Marks in connection with the Rae Mine. The Recorder (Sir Thos. Chambers) then summed up. The jury found the accused not guilty. An extraordinary scene followed the announcement of the verdict, the spectators bursting into loud applause, against which the Recorder angrily protested, and threatened to clear the court. —Mr. Gill applied that the prosecutor should pay the costs of the defence.—The Recorder said he was obliged to grant the request, but he entirely disagreed with the verdict.—Mr. John Morley waS then found not guilty of publishing a libel.
